name: Gmail
alternative: IMAP and SMTP with an app password (needs 2-Step Verification), or Mail on the Mac through Apple Events
notes: Google's own Gmail MCP server is in the Workspace Developer Preview and needs a Google Cloud OAuth client plus restricted Gmail scopes (gmail.readonly, gmail.compose), so public use needs restricted-scope verification and a yearly security assessment. Discovery 2026-10-08: protected resource names accounts.google.com; no DCR, no CIMD, S256, client-secret token auth only; the MCP Registry lists only community Gmail servers.

name: Spotify
alternative: the person's own Development Mode app on the Web API (needs Spotify Premium, at most 5 users), or local playback control of the Spotify Mac app
notes: Spotify hosts the MCP server behind its Claude connector (Claude's listing, made by Spotify, names https://mcp-gateway-external-pilot.spotify.net/mcp; a pilot host). It returns 401 and its metadata points to accounts.spotify.com, which on 2026-10-09 advertised no DCR, no CIMD, S256 and public clients (token auth none), so Kipster needs a Spotify client ID. Web API apps beyond Development Mode (5 users, owner needs Premium, one client ID per developer) need extended quota, open only to registered businesses with at least 250k monthly users after a review of up to six weeks. The registry lists only community servers (e.g. github.com/jamiew/spotify-mcp).

name: iCloud Drive
alternative: the iCloud Drive folder synced on the person's Mac, read and written as local files (with Desktop and Documents if the person syncs them)
notes: Apple has no MCP or public web API for a person's iCloud Drive: CloudKit web services reach only an app's own CloudKit databases. The registry lists only community servers (e.g. github.com/ThomasCrouzet/icloud-mcp); files evicted by Optimize Mac Storage must download before reading.

name: Uber
alternative: Uber trip receipt emails in the person's mailbox; ride requests through Uber's Siri support on iPhone
notes: Uber's Riders API needs approval through an Uber business development contact. Uber hosts a Claude-specific connector (mcp.uber.com/claude/rides-3p/mcp, ride estimates only) that it does not document for other clients; on 2026-10-08 the endpoint refused unauthenticated requests and its discovery URLs returned no metadata, and the registry lists no Uber-owned server (community example: glama.ai 199-mcp/mcp-uber).

name: Microsoft OneDrive
alternative: the OneDrive folder synced on the person's Mac by the OneDrive app, read as local files
notes: Microsoft Graph's OneDrive API covers personal accounts, and the project registers one free Entra app with the "Personal accounts only" or personal-plus-work account type, no review. Microsoft's Work IQ OneDrive MCP (preview) is for work accounts with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, and the registry lists only community OneDrive servers (e.g. github.com/0xka13b/microsoft-mcps); consumer sign-in discovery 2026-10-08: no DCR, no CIMD advertised. No vendor page states that there is no official MCP; that rests on registry and vendor-site searches.

name: Telegram
alternative: a Telegram bot whose token the person creates with BotFather (Bot API), which sees only chats the bot is in
notes: No official Telegram MCP (registry lists only community servers, e.g. github.com/leshchenko1979/fast-mcp-telegram). The project gets one free api_id from my.telegram.org with no review and uses the MTProto API through TDLib on the Mac, with the person signing in by phone code; the API terms forbid using Telegram data to develop or deploy AI models, and unofficial clients are watched for abuse, so the terms need checking before shipping. No vendor page states that there is no official MCP; that rests on registry and vendor-site searches.

name: Reddit
alternative: the person's Reddit data request export (CSV files of their posts, comments and saved items)
notes: Reddit closed self-service Data API access in late 2025: new OAuth apps need Reddit's approval for a stated use case, and commercial use needs written approval. No official Reddit MCP was found and the registry lists only third-party servers (e.g. github.com/karanb192/reddit-mcp-buddy); discovery 2026-10-08 on www.reddit.com: no DCR, no CIMD, S256, client-secret token auth only.

name: Chase
alternative: the person's transaction download from Chase on desktop (CSV, QFX, QIF or QBO, last two years), plus Chase alert emails in their mailbox
notes: No MCP (none official or in the registry) and no self-serve consumer API: Chase shares account data only through its API with apps and data access providers that have signed data-access agreements, so a direct connection needs a partner agreement. Aggregators such as Plaid or Akoya would route the data through a third party.

name: Facebook Messenger
alternative: the person's own download of their Messenger chats (Meta's download of end-to-end encrypted chat data), read on the Mac
notes: No public API reaches a person's own Messenger chats: the Messenger Platform only lets a business Page or Instagram Professional account answer people who message it. Apps used beyond people with a role on the app need Advanced Access, which requires Meta business verification and sometimes App Review (class D for that business route). No Meta MCP for Messenger was found and the registry lists none. Meta's help article on downloading end-to-end encrypted chat data renders only with JavaScript, so its steps are unconfirmed here.

name: Todoist
alternative: Doist's local server (npx @doist/todoist-mcp) with the person's personal API token
notes: Doist hosts the official Todoist MCP server, listed in the registry as net.todoist/mcp; sign-in runs on todoist.com and the API is free, with some features limited by the person's plan. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256, token auth none or client secret.

name: Apple Photos
alternative: the Photos library on the Mac through PhotoKit or the Photos AppleScript dictionary, or Photos actions in Shortcuts
notes: Input had no website; Apple's Photos support page is used. Apple offers no web API or MCP for iCloud Photos, but PhotoKit on macOS reads the library (including iCloud Photos) after a permission prompt; community local servers exist (e.g. github.com/sweetrb/apple-photos-mcp) and nothing official is in the MCP Registry.

name: Instacart
alternative: order receipts in the person's mailbox, or Instacart's iOS app
notes: Instacart's Developer Platform MCP authenticates with the developer's API key and only creates recipe and shopping-list pages the person checks out on Instacart; production keys need an Instacart review of the integration, and the account-level shopping MCP needs an Instacart representative. Discovery 2026-10-08: no OAuth metadata (404 on mcp.instacart.com well-known paths); no Instacart-owned entry in the MCP Registry.

name: Google Flights
alternative: Google Flights price-tracking emails in the person's mailbox, or an airline's own API or app
notes: Google publishes no Google Flights API (QPX Express was retired) and lists no flights server among its official MCP servers; registry entries such as com.pulsemcp/google-flights and com.hasdata/google-flights are third-party scrapers or SerpAPI wrappers, which route queries through someone else's service. Reading price-alert emails through the person's mail plugin is the realistic route.

name: Robinhood
alternative: the person's account statements and tax documents downloaded from Robinhood
notes: Robinhood's own Trading MCP (US only) lets an agent read the person's Robinhood accounts and trade only in a separate Agentic account the person opens and funds; Robinhood names "any localhost platform" as a supported client and charges no extra fee. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256, token auth none; registry entries named Robinhood are community (e.g. io.github.verygoodplugins/robinhood-mcp).

name: Strava
alternative: the person's own Strava API app (Standard tier, needs a Strava subscription), Strava's bulk account export, or workouts Strava writes to Apple Health
notes: Strava's read-only MCP needs a Strava subscription and Strava says only Claude is supported for now, so other clients depend on Strava opening it up; the API's Standard tier (up to 10 athletes without review) also needs a subscription since 2026 and forbids routing data through intermediary platforms. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD and PKCE methods not advertised, issuer www.strava.com; no Strava-owned entry in the MCP Registry.

name: Duolingo
alternative: the download of all the person's personal data that Duolingo's Data Vault (drive-thru.duolingo.com) offers after sign-in, plus Duolingo's streak and practice emails in the person's mailbox
notes: Duolingo publishes no consumer API, developer programme or MCP server; community servers (e.g. github.com/Tavaresiqueira/duo-metrics-mcp) call undocumented web endpoints with the person's session and can break without notice, so they are excluded. No Duolingo-owned entry in the MCP Registry. Duolingo's Data Vault page states it lets a person download all personal data Duolingo stores; the file format and delivery time are unconfirmed (shown only after sign-in), and email contents are unconfirmed.

name: Goodreads
alternative: the person's library export (CSV from My Books, Import and export), read on the Mac
notes: Goodreads (Amazon) stopped issuing developer keys on 2020-12-08 and is retiring its old API, so there is no API or official MCP; community servers (e.g. github.com/Danathar/goodreads-mcp, the only registry entry) rely on scraping or old keys. The CSV export keeps data on the Mac but is read-only and as fresh as the last export.

name: Apple Passwords
alternative: a CSV file the person exports from the Passwords app on the Mac (one password or all), handed to the kip deliberately and deleted afterwards
notes: Input had no website; Apple's Passwords user guide is used. No web API or MCP, the Passwords app has no AppleScript dictionary, and Keychain Services gives an app only its own items. Apple documents a CSV export, but the file is unencrypted and Apple warns to delete it after use, so only a single deliberately chosen password should be shared.

name: Microsoft Copilot
alternative: the CSV of the person's Copilot app activity history exported from the Microsoft privacy dashboard (Export all activity history)
notes: The consumer Copilot app has no public API or MCP; Microsoft's Copilot APIs and the registry's Work IQ Copilot server (com.microsoft/workiq-m365copilot) are tenant-scoped Microsoft 365 products that need a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. For personal Microsoft accounts, Microsoft documents a CSV export of Copilot activity history from the privacy dashboard.

name: SmartThings
alternative: a SmartThings personal access token the person creates (valid only 24 hours), or SmartThings devices shared to Apple Home and reached through Home actions in Shortcuts
notes: No official MCP and nothing in the MCP Registry (community servers are listed on Glama; not reviewed here). SmartThings' public API uses OAuth with a client secret and public HTTPS redirect URIs, and its docs say API Access App registration is "coming soon and is not yet available", while personal access tokens now last 24 hours.

name: PlayStation
alternative: PlayStation Store receipt emails in the person's mailbox, or a copy of their data through Sony's privacy right-of-access request
notes: No official MCP and no public PSN API; Sony's developer access is the partner-only PlayStation Partners programme. Community tools (e.g. github.com/murzin-ml/mcp-ps-store, psn-api, Home Assistant's PlayStation Network integration) use the app's internal API with the person's NPSSO browser token and can break with any update.

name: AT&T
alternative: the person's PDF bills downloaded from myAT&T, or AT&T Bill Ready emails in their mailbox
notes: No MCP (none official or in the registry) and no API for a person's own account, bills or usage; AT&T's developer offerings (API Marketplace messaging and voice, enterprise and invite-only network APIs) are for businesses building products. myAT&T lets the person download PDF bills, which Kipster can read locally.

name: Yelp
alternative: Apple Maps place search through MapKit on the Mac for business details, without Yelp reviews
notes: Yelp's own local MCP server wraps the Yelp AI API, which needs an API key from a developer app: a 30-day trial (business email required), then $25 per 1,000 calls with a minimum of 1,000 daily calls; the Places API plans also start at a monthly fee. It searches public business data only, not the person's own Yelp account; registry entries named yelp are third-party (HasData, Pipeworx, Apify).

name: HBO Max
alternative: a copy of the person's data (including viewing activity) through HBO Max's Individual Rights access request, read locally
notes: No MCP (none official or in the registry) and no public developer API for HBO Max accounts, watch history or the catalogue; its documented Siri support covers search and playback (e.g. on Vision Pro), with no documented Shortcuts actions. The only self-serve route to the person's own data is the privacy access request.

name: Canva
alternative: a Developer Portal app on Canva's self-serve MCP URL https://api.canva.com/connect/v1/mcp (client ID and secret; a public app still needs Canva's review), or designs the person exports as PDF or PNG
notes: Canva hosts the MCP server, but a CIMD client's redirect URI must be added to Canva's MCP allowlist through a reviewed waitlist (DCR is deprecated there), and Developer Portal public apps are reviewed before release; most tools work on free plans, with resize, autofill and brand kits on Pro. Discovery 2026-10-08: mcp.canva.com DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256 and plain, token auth none allowed; api.canva.com MCP uses www.canva.com (pre-registered clients only, S256).

name: Twitch
alternative: the official Twitch CLI for a person's own testing
notes: No official Twitch MCP; registry entries are third-party (e.g. github.com/pipeworx-io/mcp-twitch, a hosted gateway that would route data through its cloud). The project registers one free app in the Twitch developer console (2FA required, no review) and can use a public client with the device code flow, so no secret ships with Kipster; OIDC discovery 2026-10-08 lists only client_secret_post and no DCR or CIMD. No vendor page states that there is no official MCP; that rests on registry and vendor-site searches.

name: Citymapper
alternative: Apple Maps transit travel times through MapKit on the Mac, or Citymapper's Siri directions on the iPhone through App Intents
notes: No MCP (none official or in the registry). Citymapper discontinued its self-service APIs and SDKs on 23 June 2023, leaving only existing Enterprise contracts; its iPhone app works with Siri for directions, which a Kipster iPhone app could only reach through App Intents (unconfirmed).

name: Whole Foods Market
alternative: Whole Foods and Amazon order and receipt emails in the person's mailbox, or a copy of their data through the privacy request form
notes: No MCP (none official or in the registry) and no public API for shoppers; online orders, Prime deals and pickup run through the person's Amazon account, which has no consumer order API either. The privacy notice offers access requests through an online form, so receipts and order emails are the practical source.

name: Bluesky
alternative: an app password with the AT Protocol API
notes: No official Bluesky MCP; community servers exist (e.g. github.com/cyanheads/bluesky-mcp-server, github.com/brianellin/bsky-mcp-server). AT Protocol OAuth uses a client ID metadata URL instead of registration, with PAR and DPoP required; discovery 2026-10-08 on bsky.social: no DCR, CIMD yes, S256, token auth none or private_key_jwt. No vendor page states that there is no official MCP; that rests on registry and vendor-site searches.

alternative: the person's transaction and statement download (CSV, Quicken or QuickBooks) from their Amex account
notes: No MCP and no self-serve consumer API: Card Member data is shared only with financial service providers Amex has connected, and developer APIs (e.g. Sync) need a partner application and approval. Statement and activity downloads keep the data on the Mac; data aggregators would route it through a third party.

name: Wyze
alternative: Apple Home for Wyze devices that support it
notes: No MCP (none official or listed in the registry). Wyze lets a person create a free API key and key ID in its Developer API Console; a script exchanges them, with the account email and password, for access and refresh tokens. The device API beyond sign-in is undocumented, so a plugin relies on community wrappers and may break.

name: Weather Underground
alternative: a free contributor API key for people who upload a personal weather station; otherwise Apple WeatherKit for forecasts
notes: No MCP and nothing in the MCP Registry. The Weather Company documents a limited API set for personal weather station contributors, with keys issued on a page behind sign-in (that these keys are free is not stated on a public vendor page); everyone else needs a paid Weather Company Data API package (Standard from $500 a month) after a 30-day trial.

name: Feedly
alternative: the person's OPML export of their sources, read locally with the feeds fetched directly
notes: Feedly's MCP server reaches its Threat Graph (threat intelligence) and is included only in the sales-led Threat Intelligence Advanced plan; it does not cover personal reading feeds, and Feedly API tokens are Enterprise-only. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256, token auth none allowed.

name: USPS
alternative: USPS tracking and Informed Delivery emails in the person's mailbox
notes: No MCP (none official or in the registry). The project creates a free USPS Business Account, registers an app and uses its consumer key and secret (OAuth client credentials) for the default APIs, which include Tracking and Addresses; higher quotas and label APIs need a service request or approval, and there is no API for a person's own Informed Delivery data.

name: Monarch Money
alternative: the person's transaction and balance CSV export from Monarch
notes: Monarch runs its own MCP server, but its help page says it has been paused since June 29 at a data provider's request, so it cannot be connected until restored; Monarch itself is a paid subscription. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256, token auth none allowed.

name: Adobe Acrobat
alternative: Adobe PDF Services API with free self-serve credentials (500 document transactions a month), or local PDF tools on the Mac
notes: Adobe runs an Acrobat MCP endpoint on adobe.io and brings Acrobat tools to Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini through its own connectors (free Adobe account or guest); Adobe's help pages blocked fetching, so whether any client may register and how long sessions last is unconfirmed. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256, token auth none only, authorization_code grant only (no refresh token advertised).

name: E*TRADE
alternative: the person's own E*TRADE consumer key used only for their account, or statements and transaction downloads from their E*TRADE account
notes: No MCP (none official or in the registry). E*TRADE's API (accounts, balances, transactions, portfolio, quotes, orders) uses OAuth 1.0a with a consumer key issued through E*TRADE's developer site after agreements and approval, callback URLs must be registered with E*TRADE, and access tokens expire at midnight US Eastern; the key process could not be read (developer.etrade.com blocked fetching).

notes: No official MCP (registry has none; community github.com/markswendsen-code/mcp-nextdoor automates the website through a hosted browser, and Pipedream's server routes data through a third party). Nextdoor's APIs are for partners: you apply and the Partnerships team issues a client ID and secret; discovery 2026-10-08 at auth.nextdoor.com (OpenID config): no DCR, no CIMD, no PKCE advertised. No vendor page states that there is no official MCP; that rests on registry and vendor-site searches.

Personal vaults have no API: the open-source CLI is the only programmatic route, and the public API is read-only team data for Business admins.

notes: Any.do's own help centre documents a free remote MCP server at https://mcp.any.do/sse (beta, all users) for tasks, reminders, workspaces and calendar; it is not in the MCP Registry. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256, token auth none allowed; the protected resource metadata sits at the /sse-suffixed path.

notes: No official MCP (registry hits are unrelated airline Wi-Fi trackers). Class C because Starlink's documented API (account, service lines, data usage) is limited to Enterprise accounts: an account admin creates a service account and exchanges its client ID and secret for a token (discovery 2026-10-09 at starlink.com/api/auth: client_credentials grant, no DCR, no CIMD, S256 and plain). notes: No MCP (none official, none in the MCP Registry). Moovit's Transit APIs are volume-metered B2B products sold through sales contact, with no self-serve keys and no access to a person's account or saved trips; the API sign-in method is not publicly documented.

notes: No official MCP or public developer API for shopping or IKEA accounts; community servers (e.g. glama listings david-s-svedberg/ikea-mcp, taejin5314/ikea-mcp) scrape the storefront and are not in the MCP Registry. notes: No MCP (none official or in the MCP Registry) and no published developer API: the Life360 help centre (which now hosts Tile support) has no API article and lists Tile's third-party integrations as discontinued, and Home Assistant relies on pytile, an unofficial library for an unpublished API. alternative: Glassdoor job-alert and saved-job emails in the person's mailbox; the person's data export under the privacy policy
notes: No official MCP: the only MCP Registry entry (com.hasdata/glassdoor) is a third-party scraping service that routes requests through HasData's cloud. Glassdoor's former public API endpoint (api.glassdoor.com/api/api.htm) now answers 410 Gone, and its developer and help pages blocked automated reading, so no current partner programme was confirmed.

notes: No MCP (none official or in the MCP Registry) and no public consumer API: Ally's help centre offers only manual CSV or QFX downloads, and the former Ally Invest API documentation URL now redirects to the Ally Invest marketing page. notes: No official MCP (community servers such as atfinke/loseit-mcp and cabird/loseit-mcp on Glama; none in the MCP Registry). notes: No MCP (none official or in the registry) and no public API: the old developer.iheart.com programme is offline. notes: Shopify hosts an official Shop MCP server (catalog search, carts, Shop Pay checkout, order tracking); search works anonymously and signing in adds addresses, orders and purchase approvals. notes: Website was empty in the input; Apple's Numbers page is used. Numbers has no web API or official MCP (registry has only a community macOS server, github.com/aernouddekker/macos-mcp), so a plugin scripts Numbers on the Mac through Apple Events and its Shortcuts and Siri actions, per ios.md.

notes: Shipt's own MCP server powers its Claude connector (sign-in required) and ChatGPT app, launched August 2026 as partner integrations; Shipt has no public developer API. notes: Thumbtack hosts the MCP server behind its Claude connector (search pros, reviews, categories; its scopes also cover prices and requests), but it returns 401 without a token. notes: No MCP (none in the registry) and no public developer API found: USAA shares account data only with apps and companies that connect directly with it, which means partner data-access agreements. Statement downloads keep data on the Mac; data aggregators would route it through a third party.

No Omni page states that OmniFocus has no web API; that rests on searches of Omni's site.

name: Mint Mobile
alternative: plan renewal and billing emails in the person's mailbox; usage and balance stay in the Mint Mobile app
notes: No public API, developer programme or MCP (none official, none in the registry); account management is only in the Mint Mobile app and website. mintmobile.com blocked automated fetches (Cloudflare), so the absence of an API is confirmed only from the App Store listing and searches.

name: Day One
alternative: Day One's Shortcuts actions or its dayone CLI on the Mac
notes: Day One's official MCP server is built into the Mac app's CLI (`dayone mcp`, stdio), reads and writes the local journal store with per-journal opt-in, and needs no sign-in; it requires a Silver or Gold subscription and app 2026.17+, and will not start while password lock is on. No hosted MCP or web API; Mac only. No entry in the MCP Registry.

name: Grindr
alternative: the person's Grindr data download (Settings > Download My Data), read on the Mac
notes: No public API, developer programme or MCP (none official, none in the registry); Grindr discourages third-party apps for data access. Its in-app data download is the only workable route, read-only and as fresh as the last request; dating chats are highly sensitive data to send to AI providers.

name: Kraken

notes: No official MCP and no public API; Clue syncs with Apple Health only with the person's approval and offers a portable copy of their data on request. Cycle data is sensitive health data.

name: VA
alternative: the Veteran's own Blue Button health record download from My HealtheVet
notes: No official MCP; VA's API platform offers Veteran-authorized OAuth APIs (health records, claims, service history, disability rating) with free sandbox keys, but production access needs a VA application and review. Discovery 2026-10-08: no registration endpoint, S256, public clients allowed.

name: Rome2Rio
alternative: none
notes: Rome2Rio runs its own remote MCP server (route and timetable lookup, read-only) listed in Claude's connector directory with sign-in not required. Direct probes of the endpoint were blocked by Cloudflare, so the open-access claim rests on the directory listing.

name: Financial Times
alternative: the person's myFT RSS feed of the topics they follow (switched on in FT account contact preferences), plus FT's public RSS headline feeds
notes: No official MCP (none in the MCP Registry). FT API keys come only with a licence agreement that sets fees (e.g. the Datamining Licence), so there is no personal reader API. FT documents a myFT RSS feed of followed topics that carries no personal information; full articles need an FT subscription.

name: Wanderlog
alternative: the person's trip plan printed from the Wanderlog website and saved as a PDF through the Mac's Print dialog (manual, one trip at a time)
notes: Wanderlog has no public API; the only MCP is community repo shaikhspeare/wanderlog-mcp, which reuses the browser session cookie against Wanderlog's private web API and is not endorsed. name: Levels.fyi
alternative: Public Levels.fyi salary pages read in the browser
notes: Official remote MCP with DCR and S256 PKCE, but it is included only in Levels.fyi Enterprise data plans requested with a corporate email; individuals have no self-serve access. Community packages such as levels-fyi-mcp on PyPI are unofficial.

name: Tomorrow.io
alternative: Tomorrow.io REST Weather API with the same key
notes: Official hosted MCP authenticated with the person's own Tomorrow.io API key in an X-Api-Key header. A free self-serve plan with rate limits is widely documented, but its exact quota and whether every MCP tool works on it were not confirmed.

name: Polarsteps
alternative: The person's Polarsteps data archive (JSON, requested in account settings and emailed as a download link)
notes: Polarsteps has no public API; community repo remuzel/polarsteps-mcp uses undocumented APIs with the browser remember_token cookie. The self-service JSON archive is the workable route, read-only and as fresh as the last export.

name: Edison Mail
alternative: IMAP and SMTP to the person's underlying mail provider with an app-specific password (Edison Mail is only a client for those accounts)
notes: Edison Mail is a mail client with no public developer API or MCP; the mail itself lives at the person's provider (Gmail, iCloud, Outlook, Yahoo...), which Kipster can reach directly over IMAP/SMTP or that provider's own plugin.

name: realestate.com.au
alternative: realestate.com.au's own saved-search and property alert emails in the person's mailbox, read through the mail plugin
notes: No MCP (no REA server in the MCP Registry). REA's Partner Platform APIs serve agency software, need partner onboarding for credentials and support only OAuth client credentials (no end-user sign-in), so there is no consumer API for saved searches or shortlists. REA's App Store listing says saved searches can be received by email. No vendor page states that there is no official MCP; that rests on registry and vendor-site searches.

name: Outschool
alternative: Outschool's personal ICS calendar feeds (enrolled, favourited and teaching classes)
notes: Outschool has no public developer API or MCP; its partnerships are for schools and employers. Each account can subscribe to personal ICS feeds, which give a read-only view of the class schedule.

name: ViX
alternative: ViX Premium payment receipt emails in the person's mailbox (subscription status only)
notes: ViX (TelevisaUnivision) publishes no developer API or MCP and its help centre documents no Shortcuts actions, so the watchlist and history are not reachable. ViX's help centre says Premium subscribers in the US and other countries get a payment receipt by email; app-store and partner subscriptions are billed by those companies.

name: OKX
alternative: OKX REST API with the same key
notes: OKX's own Agent Trade Kit ships a local MCP server (npm @okx_ai/okx-trade-mcp) that uses the person's self-created OKX API key, kept on the Mac, with a --read-only flag for query-only tools. Trading tools can move real funds, so Kipster should default to read-only keys.

name: SpotHero

notes: No MCP (none in the MCP Registry). SpotHero's FAQ says each booking sends an email confirmation with the Parking Pass, so a kip can read the person's reservations from the mailbox. No vendor page states that there is no official MCP; that rests on registry and vendor-site searches.

notes: Beeper Desktop has a built-in MCP server and REST API on localhost:23373 (/v0/mcp), also wrapped by Beeper's npm package @beeper/desktop-mcp, authorised with a token the person creates in Settings > Integrations or with local OAuth plus PKCE. Beeper Desktop must be running on the Mac; messages bridged from other networks still pass through Beeper's own servers as part of the service.

name: Heptabase
alternative: Heptabase CLI or the person's Heptabase backup export
notes: Official remote MCP (read, search, create and edit cards, journals and whiteboards). Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256; scopes space:read and space:write. Heptabase itself is a paid subscription after its trial.

name: Chirp
alternative: Chirp order receipt and confirmation emails in the person's mailbox (books bought, prices)
notes: Chirp (from the BookBub team) has no public developer API or MCP; its partner programme is for publishers submitting deals. name: Telstra
alternative: Telstra email bills in the person's mailbox (amounts, due dates, charges)
notes: No MCP and no API for a customer's own account (bills, usage, plan); Telstra's developer APIs such as the Messaging (SMS) API are separate paid business products. notes: Remini (Bending Spoons) publishes no developer API or MCP; remini.ai redirects to the consumer web app. Its help centre documents a data request that returns a portable electronic list of personal data (not uploaded images) and says downloaded results go to the device gallery; the data copy's format is unconfirmed.

alternative: none

name: Hims & Hers

notes: No MCP and no API for a subscriber's own account (plan, data usage, bills); Jio's developer platform only covers apps for the Jio set-top box. Jio's FAQ says every postpaid user receives an e-bill PDF at their registered email; prepaid recharge emails are unconfirmed.

alternative: Cambly reservation confirmation and lesson reminder emails in the person's mailbox, added to their calendar through the calendar plugin
notes: Cambly publishes no developer API or MCP (no developer or API pages on its site). Its help centre says students get emails to confirm reserved lessons and several reminders before each reservation, which a kip can read from the mailbox; recordings and tutor chats stay in Cambly's own apps.

alternative: Ro shipment and refill emails in the person's mailbox
notes: Ro is a US telehealth company with no public developer API or MCP found; treatment plans, prescriptions and messages with providers stay in Ro's own app. Ro emails patients about shipments and refills, but ro.co blocked automated fetching, so email contents and the absence of an API are unconfirmed from Ro itself.

name: CNBC
alternative: CNBC's own public RSS feeds (headlines and links, e.g. Top News)

notes: ParentSquare offers no public API for parents; the only MCP server (github.com/thehesiod/psquare-mcp, unaffiliated) scrapes the web app with session cookies and may breach the terms. School notices also arrive by email, which Kipster can read through the person's mail.

name: Kaiser Permanente
alternative: health records the person downloads from kp.org, or clinical records in Apple Health on the Mac where available
notes: No MCP server; Kaiser lets members share health and coverage data with third-party apps through its CMS Patient Access FHIR API, with apps registered through developer.kp.org (onboarding terms not readable without JavaScript, assumed reviewed).

name: Albert
alternative: Albert Cash monthly statements the person downloads from the app's Documents section
notes: Albert publishes no developer API or MCP server; its site links no developer docs and API trackers list none. Linked bank data could only be reached through aggregators, which would route it through a third party.

notes: Ecovacs publishes its own local MCP server (PyPI ecovacs-robot-mcp) for listing robots, starting cleaning, recharging and status, signed in with an access key the owner creates in the Ecovacs Open Platform console (open.ecovacs.com). name: B&H Photo
alternative: B&H order confirmation and shipping emails in the person's mailbox
notes: B&H has no public API for customers' orders or accounts and no MCP server; its product catalog feed is offered only to approved affiliates and is not a personal-data route. Order details are realistically reached through the person's own order emails.

name: PG&E
alternative: Green Button Download My Data files (CSV or XML) the customer exports from their PG&E account
notes: No MCP server; PG&E's Share My Data API (Green Button Connect, ESPI) needs a third-party registration that PG&E approves, a CA-issued certificate and a server notification URI, which does not suit a Mac-only app. The customer's own Green Button usage export is the practical route; PG&E's pages block automated fetching.

name: Mercado Pago

notes: Mercado Pago hosts an official MCP server (beta) for developers and sellers: docs search, app and credential management, webhooks, test users and integration checks, not the person's live payments. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256, public clients.

name: Priority Pass
alternative: membership and lounge-visit emails in the person's mailbox, plus the public lounge directory on prioritypass.com
notes: Priority Pass (Collinson) offers no public developer API or MCP server; its integrations are for card issuers and other business partners only. Visit receipts and membership details reach the person by email.

name: Badoo
alternative: A copy of the person's Badoo data requested through Badoo's support chat (Subject Access Request), read from the file it returns
notes: Badoo (Bumble Inc.) offers no public developer API or MCP server. Badoo's help centre documents a data request through chat support, answered within a month, giving a one-off snapshot of account data and conversations; the file format is not stated.

name: The Athletic
alternative: The Athletic's public RSS headline feeds
notes: The Athletic (New York Times) has no API or MCP server of its own, and no account or subscription access for third parties; the free NYT developer APIs cover Times journalism, not confirmed for Athletic content. Its public RSS feed gives headlines and links.

name: Autotrader
alternative: Autotrader saved-search and saved-car alert emails (new matches, price drops) in the person's mailbox
notes: No MCP server and no consumer API; Cox Automotive's APIs, including Autotrader inventory and deal services, are partner-gated after review by a Cox account representative and aimed at dealers. Autotrader announced email alerts for a shopper's saved searches and saved cars (new inventory, price cuts), which a kip can read from the mailbox; the current alert format is unconfirmed because autotrader.com help pages blocked fetching.

name: BMO
alternative: transactions the person downloads from BMO Online Banking (CSV, or Quicken/QuickBooks formats)
notes: BMO offers no public consumer API or MCP server; account data reaches third parties only through partner aggregators, which would route it through someone else's cloud. Online Banking lets customers download deposit and credit card transactions (up to about 123 days) for local reading.

name: SmartHQ
alternative: none
notes: No MCP server; GE Appliances' SmartHQ Developer Portal offers cloud APIs (Digital Twin, pub/sub) with OAuth 2.0 and self-created apps with a client ID and secret, as community Homebridge plugins use. Whether a widely distributed app needs GE review is not documented in readable pages.

name: AwardWallet

notes: No official MCP; the unaffiliated github.com/bbarabe/awardwallet-mcp runs locally on AwardWallet's Account Access API with a key the person creates in a free linked AwardWallet Business account. name: PressReader
alternative: subscription invoices the person opens from Payment History on pressreader.com and saves as files (manual; billing only, not reading history)
notes: No MCP server; PressReader's developer portal (Azure API Management) shows no public API products and requires sign-up for subscription keys, which points to partner-only access; not confirmed from documentation. Its help centre documents saving each invoice from the account's Payment History, a thin billing-only route; no Shortcuts actions or reading-history export are documented.

name: PictureThis
alternative: single plant identifications the person exports through the app's Share button, and plant photos saved one at a time (manual, per item)
notes: PictureThis (Glority) publishes no developer API or MCP server. Its FAQ documents sharing a saved identification to a chosen channel and saving single photos, so the route is manual and per item; no bulk export or Shortcuts actions are documented, and care reminders stay in the app.

name: PowerSchool
alternative: PowerSchool Parent Portal email notifications (grade and attendance summaries, assignment scores, attendance detail) in the parent's mailbox
notes: No official MCP; community servers (e.g. github.com/443pablo/mcp-powerschool) need each district's administrator to install a PowerSchool plugin and issue OAuth client credentials, so a parent cannot connect alone. PowerSchool's parent documentation describes Email Notifications that send grade and attendance reports daily to monthly, which a kip can read from the mailbox; a district can disable features.

name: DigiLocker
alternative: document PDFs the person downloads from their DigiLocker wallet to the Mac
notes: No MCP server; DigiLocker's Requester APIs (OAuth through API Setu) are only for registered Partner Organizations onboarded as Requesters under DigiLocker's partner SOP, not for individual apps without that approval. Citizens can download their own issued documents for local use.

name: ING
alternative: transactions the person exports from ING online banking (CSV, or MT940/CAMT where offered) and reads on the Mac
notes: No MCP server; ING's account APIs on its developer portal are PSD2 open-banking APIs for regulator-licensed third parties with eIDAS certificates, not available to an unlicensed app. Aggregators that hold such licences would route the data through a third party; the portal is JavaScript-only, so requirements are not confirmed here.

name: Coupang

notes: No official MCP and no API for shoppers' orders; Coupang's Open API is for sellers, who issue HMAC access keys in Coupang Wing with an IP allowlist. Community MCP servers listed on Glama (e.g. uju777/coupang-mcp) are unofficial and some drive a browser.

name: Whirlpool

notes: Whirlpool publishes no developer API or MCP server, and its App Store listing names voice assistants but no Siri Shortcuts or Apple Home support. Its privacy page documents a Data Access webform for residents of California, Colorado, Texas, Virginia and other listed US states or Canada: a one-off snapshot, not live appliance state. Home Assistant's integration signs in with the person's Whirlpool password against an undocumented cloud API, which Kipster must not use.

name: TaxAct

notes: TaxAct hosts an official MCP server (registry namespace com.taxact) for tax filing guidance, cost comparison, document checklists and refund estimates; it needs no sign-in and does not reach the person's return. name: Ecosia

notes: No public search API or MCP server found for third parties, and ecosia.org sits behind a bot firewall that blocks automated requests. Ecosia's help centre documents bookmark export from its desktop browser and iOS and Android apps; Ecosia accounts otherwise hold little personal data.

name: Yousician

notes: No official MCP server and no public developer API found; the app's own backend API is private. Yousician documents a self-serve archive of profile and gameplay history; its file format is not stated.

name: Samsung Food

notes: No official MCP server; the Whisk Partners API behind Samsung Food (with per-user OAuth tokens) needs a Whisk business agreement and Whisk no longer accepts new sandbox applications. Its help centre documents printing a shopping list, which Save as PDF on the Mac turns into a file, and read-only sharing by invitation; no personal data export or Siri actions are documented.

name: Snapseed
alternative: edited photos the person exports as flattened JPEGs to the Photos library, reachable on the Mac through PhotoKit
notes: Google's Snapseed is an on-device photo editor with no web API or MCP server found, and its App Store listing shows no Siri or Shortcuts support. Google's help documents Export, which saves a flattened JPEG to the Camera Roll that other apps can read.

name: BBVA

notes: No official MCP server; BBVA API_Market serves businesses and regulatory PSD2 APIs open only to licensed third-party providers, so there is no consumer self-serve API. BBVA documents statement download (PDF in Mexico) and Siri balance and Bizum actions in the Spain app; Excel or CSV movement exports are unconfirmed because bbva.es blocks automated requests.

name: SimpleLogin
alternative: none
notes: No official MCP server (community: enthouan/simplelogin-mcp); SimpleLogin's documented REST API takes an API key the person creates in their account, for listing and creating aliases, mailboxes and contacts.

name: BAND

notes: No official MCP server and no public web API for learner progress (staff have only ever described one as planned). freeCodeCamp settings offer a Download your data button that saves the signed-in account record as JSON; its exact contents are unconfirmed.

notes: Amazon Flex is a delivery-partner app with no public API or MCP server, and earnings are shown in the app's Earnings section; no earnings email or self-service export is documented. Its privacy notice offers access requests to transportation-privacy@amazon.com where law requires, and Amazon's state privacy disclosures document access in a portable format through Request Your Personal Information: a one-off snapshot, limited to applicable US states, and whether it includes Flex earnings is unconfirmed. notes: No official MCP server and no public consumer API for BookMyShow bookings or listings; integrations are partner arrangements and the site blocks automated fetching. BookMyShow's support centre documents booking confirmations by SMS, WhatsApp and email.
